question: Will Catalina Lauf be the Republican nominee for FL-19?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Republican Party to contest the FL-19 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Republican primary will take place on August 18, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Republican sources, including https://www.rnc.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

evidence.excerpt: Republican candidates in the District 19 congressional race were spending millions on television ads, mailers and online promotion, with much of the money coming from their own pockets. Catalina Lauf had raised the most in individual donations, $1.4 million through June 30, without lending her campaign money. President Trump had given no indication that he would endorse a candidate, and Florida Gulf Coast University political scientist Bethany Conrad said voters were waiting for an endorsement from Trump or Byron Donalds. The article listed August 8–15 for early voting and August 18 for the primary.

Associated Builders and Contractors Florida Gulf Coast Chapter endorsed Catalina Lauf for Congressional District 19 as part of a slate of Republican congressional candidates. Lauf was one of 10 Republicans who qualified for the district’s primary ballot. Other candidates included Madison Cawthorn, Chris Collins, Jim Schwartzel and Jim Oberweis.

An Action Solutions survey conducted for Ola Hawatmeh’s campaign found Hawatmeh at 12.9%, Chris Collins at 11.8% and Jim Schwartzel at 10.2%. The largest group was undecided or supporting someone else. The sample contained 96 respondents, of whom just 45 expressed a candidate preference.

Victory Insights found Jim Schwartzel at about 13% and Jim Oberweis just below 12%, the only candidates in double digits. Catalina Lauf was just below 5%, while nearly 54% of voters remained undecided. The poll’s margin of error was 5.2 percentage points. Lauf was known to 39% of respondents, compared with almost 55% for Oberweis and 48% for Schwartzel.

The Republican Party of Florida announced congressional debates for Florida’s 19th and 25th districts on June 27, 2026, at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino. Ola Hawatmeh and Madison Cawthorn were confirmed participants in the District 19 debate. Chris Collins, Catalina Lauf, Jim Oberweis and Jim Schwartzel had also been invited.

U.S. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna endorsed Catalina Lauf for the open Southwest Florida congressional seat. Lauf had also received endorsements from U.S. Rep. Burgess Owens and U.S. Sen. Jim Banks. Lauf previously lost the 2020 Republican primary in Illinois’ 14th Congressional District to Jim Oberweis, who was again competing against her in FL-19.
